findings.title: [TOMCAT-MGR-001] Apache Tomcat Manager Console & Credential Verification on 192.168.195.139:8080
findings.description: Safe PoC check `TOMCAT-MGR-001` verified Apache Tomcat Manager console exposure at `http://192.168.195.139:8080/manager/html` (`default_credentials_success`). Post-exploitation verification confirmed administrative application list visibility without altering target state.
findings.remediation: Disable `/manager/html` on untrusted interfaces, remove default `tomcat:tomcat` credentials in `tomcat-users.xml`, and enforce IP allowlisting.

findings.title: [SMB-LIST-001] Anonymous SMB Share Enumeration Verified on 192.168.195.139:445
findings.description: Safe PoC exploitation check `SMB-LIST-001` established an unauthenticated SMB null-session to `192.168.195.139:445` and enumerated the following network shares: IPC$, ADMIN$, print$, tmp. Post-exploitation impact confirmed unauthorized disclosure of share topology.
findings.remediation: Disable SMB null sessions (RestrictAnonymous=1 / RestrictNullSessAccess=1), enforce SMBv3 packet signing, and require authenticated ACLs on all shares.

findings.title: [OWASP ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description:
Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.

[Standard]: WASC-15 | OWASP: OWASP_2021_A05 | Affected Endpoints: 15
findings.remediation: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [OWASP ZAP] Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
findings.description:
The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options.

[Standard]: WASC-15 | OWASP: OWASP_2021_A05 | Affected Endpoints: 15
findings.remediation:
Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.

findings.title: [OWASP ZAP] Application Error Disclosure
findings.description:
This page contains an error/warning message that may disclose sensitive information like the location of the file that produced the unhandled exception. This information can be used to launch further attacks against the web application. The alert could be a false positive if the error message is found inside a documentation page.

[Standard]: WASC-13 | OWASP: OWASP_2021_A05 | Affected Endpoints: 11
findings.remediation: Review the source code of this page. Implement custom error pages. Consider implementing a mechanism to provide a unique error reference/identifier to the client (browser) while logging the details on the server side and not exposing them to the user.

findings.title: [OWASP ZAP] Directory Browsing
findings.description:
It is possible to view a listing of the directory contents. Directory listings may reveal hidden scripts, include files, backup source files, etc., which can be accessed to reveal sensitive information.

[Standard]: WASC-16 | OWASP: OWASP_2021_A05 | Affected Endpoints: 9
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to disable directory browsing.

findings.title: [OWASP ZAP] Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens
findings.description:
No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in a HTML submission form.
A cross-site request forgery is an attack that involves forcing a victim to send an HTTP request to a target destination without their knowledge or intent in order to perform an action as the victim. The underlying cause is application functionality using predictable URL/form actions in a repeatable way. The nature of the attack is that CSRF exploits the trust that a web site has for a user. By contrast, cross-site scripting (XSS) exploits the trust that a user has for a web site. Like XSS, CSRF attacks are not necessarily cross-site, but they can be. Cross-site request forgery is also known as CSRF, XSRF, one-click attack, session riding, confused deputy, and sea surf.

CSRF attacks are effective in a number of situations, including:
    * The victim has an active session on the target site.
    * The victim is authenticated via HTTP auth on the target site.
    * The victim is on the same local network as the target site.

CSRF has primarily been used to perform an action against a target site using the victim's privileges, but recent techniques have been discovered to disclose information by gaining access to the response. The risk of information disclosure is dramatically increased when the target site is vulnerable to XSS, because XSS can be used as a platform for CSRF, allowing the attack to operate within the bounds of the same-origin policy.

[Standard]: WASC-9 | OWASP: OWASP_2021_A01 | Affected Endpoints: 8
findings.remediation:
Phase: Architecture and Design
Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid.
For example, use anti-CSRF packages such as the OWASP CSRFGuard.

Phase: Implementation
Ensure that your application is free of cross-site scripting issues, because most CSRF defenses can be bypassed using attacker-controlled script.

Phase: Architecture and Design
Generate a unique nonce for each form, place the nonce into the form, and verify the nonce upon receipt of the form. Be sure that the nonce is not predictable (CWE-330).
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Identify especially dangerous operations. When the user performs a dangerous operation, send a separate confirmation request to ensure that the user intended to perform that operation.
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Use the ESAPI Session Management control.
This control includes a component for CSRF.

Do not use the GET method for any request that triggers a state change.

Phase: Implementation

findings.title: [OWASP ZAP] X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
findings.description:
The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing.

[Standard]: WASC-15 | OWASP: OWASP_2021_A05 | Affected Endpoints: 15
findings.remediation:
Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.
If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that does not perform MIME-sniffing at all, or that can be directed by the web application/web server to not perform MIME-sniffing.

attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to tcp://192.168.195.139:139 can leverage 'Nmap Deep Fingerprint: Samba smbd 3.X - 4.X (139/TCP)' (CWE-200) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'tcp://192.168.195.139:139'.

remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'tcp://192.168.195.139:139' are rejected or redirected.

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

validation.test_name: Outdated Software Banner CVE & Template Verification
validation.methodology: Correlates fingerprinted software versions with Nmap NSE and Nuclei CVE verification templates.
validation.expected_result: Target enforces security control (CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure (Missing Security Headers)) and rejects insecure configuration.
validation.actual_result: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.
reproduction_steps: 1. Ensure target 'http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml' is within approved Rules of Engagement allowlist.
2. Issue GET request to 'http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml'.
3. Inspect response headers/body for evidence matching: ZAP-10038-10038-1.
4. Compare response against the expected secure control baseline.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml can leverage '[OWASP ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set' (CWE-693) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

remediation.root_cause: CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure (Missing Security Headers)) observed on http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml.
remediation.technical_remediation: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.
implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml'.
2. Apply recommended control: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.
3. Deploy change to staging and verify application functionality.
4. Execute TrePath deterministic retest to confirm control enforcement.
remediation.verification_procedure: Re-issue GET probe to 'http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml' and confirm ZAP-10038-10038-1 is no longer triggered.
remediation.functional_test: Verify authorized users and API clients can still access 'http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml' over approved transport.
remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'http://192.168.195.139/sitemap.xml' are rejected or redirected.

786.title: [OWASP ZAP] Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
786.proof_state_meaning: A defensive security control is demonstrably missing, weak, or misconfigured based on captured response evidence.
786.exploitability_note: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

overview.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames (Clickjacking)
overview.affected_environment: VMware Lab Pentest Engagement (http://192.168.195.139/) (Internal Testing Lab)

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior:
Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.

validation.test_name: Outdated Software Banner CVE & Template Verification
validation.methodology: Correlates fingerprinted software versions with Nmap NSE and Nuclei CVE verification templates.
validation.expected_result: Target enforces security control (CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames (Clickjacking)) and rejects insecure configuration.
validation.actual_result: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options.
reproduction_steps: 1. Ensure target 'http://192.168.195.139/twiki/' is within approved Rules of Engagement allowlist.
2. Issue GET request to 'http://192.168.195.139/twiki/' inspecting parameter/header 'x-frame-options'.
3. Inspect response headers/body for evidence matching: ZAP-10020-10020-1.
4. Compare response against the expected secure control baseline.

DISCOVERED.exploitability_note: Observation only — does not establish that an attacker exploited or can exploit the finding.

OBSERVATION_CONFIRMED.meaning: The observed network, protocol, or HTTP response behavior was deterministically captured in a forensic transcript.
OBSERVATION_CONFIRMED.exploitability_note: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

CONTROL_GAP_CONFIRMED.exploitability_note: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

ATTACK_PATH_VALIDATED.exploitability_note: Prerequisites and chaining conditions were verified.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139/twiki/ and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/twiki/ can leverage '[OWASP ZAP] Missing Anti-clickjacking Header' (CWE-1021) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect

remediation.root_cause: CWE-1021 (Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames (Clickjacking)) observed on http://192.168.195.139/twiki/.
remediation.technical_remediation:
Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.
implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'http://192.168.195.139/twiki/'.

2. Apply recommended control: Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.
3. Deploy change to staging and verify application functionality.
4. Execute TrePath deterministic retest to confirm control enforcement.

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed: This page contains an error/warning message that may disclose sensitive information like the location of the file that produced the unhandled exception. This information can be used to launch further attacks against the web application. The alert could be a false positive if the error message is found inside a documentation page.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior: Review the source code of this page. Implement custom error pages. Consider implementing a mechanism to provide a unique error reference/identifier to the client (browser) while logging the details on the server side and not exposing them to the user.

overview.cwe_name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
overview.affected_environment: VMware Lab Pentest Engagement (http://192.168.195.139/) (Internal Testing Lab)

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed:
No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in a HTML submission form.
A cross-site request forgery is an attack that involves forcing a victim to send an HTTP request to a target destination without their knowledge or intent in order to perform an action as the victim. The underlying cause is application functionality using predictable URL/form actions in a repeatable way. The nature of the attack is that CSRF exploits the trust that a web site has for a user. By contrast, cross-site scripting (XSS) exploits the trust that a user has for a web site. Like XSS, CSRF attacks are not necessarily cross-site, but they can be. Cross-site request forgery is also known as CSRF, XSRF, one-click attack, session riding, confused deputy, and sea surf.

CSRF attacks are effective in a number of situations, including:
    * The victim has an active session on the target site.
    * The victim is authenticated via HTTP auth on the target site.
    * The victim is on the same local network as the target site.

CSRF has primarily been used to perform an action against a target site using the victim's privileges, but recent techniques have been discovered to disclose information by gaining access to the response. The risk of information disclosure is dramatically increased when the target site is vulnerable to XSS, because XSS can be used as a platform for CSRF, allowing the attack to operate within the bounds of the same-origin policy.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior:
Phase: Architecture and Design
Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid.
For example, use anti-CSRF packages such as the OWASP CSRFGuard.

Phase: Implementation
Ensure that your application is free of cross-site scripting issues, because most CSRF defenses can be bypassed using attacker-controlled script.

Phase: Architecture and Design
Generate a unique nonce for each form, place the nonce into the form, and verify the nonce upon receipt of the form. Be sure that the nonce is not predictable (CWE-330).
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Identify especially dangerous operations. When the user performs a dangerous operation, send a separate confirmation request to ensure that the user intended to perform that operation.
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Use the ESAPI Session Management control.
This control includes a component for CSRF.

Do not use the GET method for any request that triggers a state change.

Phase: Implementation
Check the HTTP Referer header to see if the request originated from an expected page. This could break legitimate functionality, because users or proxies may have disabled sending the Referer for privacy reasons.

validation.expected_result: Target enforces security control (CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)) and rejects insecure configuration.
validation.actual_result:
No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in a HTML submission form.
A cross-site request forgery is an attack that involves forcing a victim to send an HTTP request to a target destination without their knowledge or intent in order to perform an action as the victim. The underlying cause is application functionality using predictable URL/form actions in a repeatable way. The nature of the attack is that CSRF exploits the trust that a web site has for a user. By contrast, cross-site scripting (XSS) exploits the trust that a user has for a web site. Like XSS, CSRF attacks are not necessarily cross-site, but they can be. Cross-site request forgery is also known as CSRF, XSRF, one-click attack, session riding, confused deputy, and sea surf.

CSRF attacks are effective in a number of situations, including:
    * The victim has an active session on the target site.
    * The victim is authenticated via HTTP auth on the target site.
    * The victim is on the same local network as the target site.

CSRF has primarily been used to perform an action against a target site using the victim's privileges, but recent techniques have been discovered to disclose information by gaining access to the response. The risk of information disclosure is dramatically increased when the target site is vulnerable to XSS, because XSS can be used as a platform for CSRF, allowing the attack to operate within the bounds of the same-origin policy.

remediation.technical_remediation:
Phase: Architecture and Design
Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid.
For example, use anti-CSRF packages such as the OWASP CSRFGuard.

Phase: Implementation
Ensure that your application is free of cross-site scripting issues, because most CSRF defenses can be bypassed using attacker-controlled script.

Phase: Architecture and Design
Generate a unique nonce for each form, place the nonce into the form, and verify the nonce upon receipt of the form. Be sure that the nonce is not predictable (CWE-330).
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Identify especially dangerous operations. When the user performs a dangerous operation, send a separate confirmation request to ensure that the user intended to perform that operation.
Note that this can be bypassed using XSS.

Use the ESAPI Session Management control.
This control includes a component for CSRF.

Do not use the GET method for any request that triggers a state change.

Phase: Implementation
Check the HTTP Referer header to see if the request originated from an expected page. This could break legitimate functionality, because users or proxies may have disabled sending the Referer for privacy reasons.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap

validation.expected_result: Target enforces security control (CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor) and rejects insecure configuration.
validation.actual_result: PHPinfo page was detected. The output of the phpinfo() command can reveal sensitive and detailed PHP environment information.
reproduction_steps: 1. Ensure target 'http://192.168.195.139//phpinfo.php' is within approved Rules of Engagement allowlist.
2. Issue GET request to 'http://192.168.195.139//phpinfo.php'.
3. Inspect response headers/body for evidence matching: NUCLEI-PHPINFO-FILES.
4. Compare response against the expected secure control baseline.

DISCOVERED.meaning: Scanner identified a possible issue or exposed surface; runtime reproduction has not yet been performed.
DISCOVERED.exploitability_note: Observation only — does not establish that an attacker exploited or can exploit the finding.

OBSERVATION_CONFIRMED.meaning: The observed network, protocol, or HTTP response behavior was deterministically captured in a forensic transcript.
OBSERVATION_CONFIRMED.exploitability_note: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

CONTROL_GAP_CONFIRMED.meaning: A defensive security control is demonstrably missing, weak, or misconfigured based on captured response evidence.
CONTROL_GAP_CONFIRMED.exploitability_note: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

ATTACK_PATH_VALIDATED.meaning: A multi-step attack path combining this weakness with reachable prerequisites was validated.
ATTACK_PATH_VALIDATED.exploitability_note: Prerequisites and chaining conditions were verified.

RUNTIME_REPRODUCED.meaning: The vulnerability was actively reproduced at runtime using a deterministic non-destructive canary or probe.
RUNTIME_REPRODUCED.exploitability_note: Runtime behavior was reproduced and verified in the response transcript.

IMPACT_VERIFIED.meaning: The downstream security impact (such as unauthorized data access or execution) was directly demonstrated.
IMPACT_VERIFIED.exploitability_note: Exploitability and security impact are cryptographically proven.

REMEDIATION_VERIFIED.meaning: Subsequent retest confirmed the security control is now properly enforced.
REMEDIATION_VERIFIED.exploitability_note: Previously observed weakness has been remediated.

NOT_VULNERABLE.meaning: Testing did not establish the suspected vulnerability.

BLOCKED_BY_SCOPE.exploitability_note: Not tested due to authorization boundary.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139//phpinfo.php and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139//phpinfo.php can leverage '[Nuclei] PHPinfo Page - Detect' (CWE-200) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap

788.title: [OWASP ZAP] X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
788.proof_state_meaning: The observed network, protocol, or HTTP response behavior was deterministically captured in a forensic transcript.
788.exploitability_note: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

overview.cwe_name: Protection Mechanism Failure (Missing Security Headers)
overview.affected_environment: VMware Lab Pentest Engagement (http://192.168.195.139/) (Internal Testing Lab)

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior:
Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.
If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that does not perform MIME-sniffing at all, or that can be directed by the web application/web server to not perform MIME-sniffing.

TWiki (TM) - A Web Based Collaboration Platform
===============================================


TWiki Distribution
------------------

Version: 01 Feb 2003
Release type: Production release


What is TWiki?
--------------

TWiki is a flexible and powerful web-based collaboration 
platform that allows you to run a dynamic intranet site, a 
project development space, a document management system, a 
knowledge base, an issue tracking system and many other 
groupware application. TWiki looks and feels like a normal 
intranet or Web site. Users can freely change or create 
content from any Web browser, without requiring special 
browser plugins. 

Major companies like Sun Microsystems, Motorola, Inktomi 
and SAP depend on the TWiki platform to increase the
productivity of their engineering teams. 

Features include automatic link generation, full text 
search, authorization based on groups, Web form handling, 
email notification of changes, file attachments to Web 
pages, revision control of pages and attachments, and 
more. The server-side TWiki Plugins API provides developers 
with a simple way to build new groupware applications. 

The GPLed TWiki software and over 60 Plugins can be 
downloaded from the TWiki.org web site, http://TWiki.org/.


TWiki Distribution and License
------------------------------

TWiki is open source software and is distributed under the 
terms of the GNU General Public License. You can request 
the latest version of TWiki from http://TWiki.org/ .

The license.txt file, located in the root of the TWiki 
distribution package, shows your rights and duties on how to 
use, redistribute and/or modify it. Any redistribution of 
TWiki or it's clones MUST contain the UNMODIFIED license.txt 
file.

Please note that TWiki is not distributed under the LGPL 
(Lesser General Public Licence), which implies TWiki can 
only be used with software that is licensed under conditions 
compliant with the GPL. Embedding in proprietary software 
requires an alternative license. Contact the author for 
details.


TWiki Installation, Support
---------------------------

It is important to follow the installation instructions in
TWikiDocumentation.html located in the distribution, also at
http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/TWiki/TWikiDocumentation

Important note: Once you installed TWiki on your own system, 
make sure to add yourself to the list of TWikiInstallations 
at http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Main/TWikiInstallations . 
This helps to get more exposure --> attract more developers 
--> result in a better product.

Please add a "Powered by TWiki" logo to your TWiki home page. 
Review details in
http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Main/PoweredByTWikiLogo

TWiki is free software and does not include any support. There
is a TWiki web for support questions, run by TWiki users for
TWiki users. Visit http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Support/ if
you have any installation questions or questions about TWiki
deployment; please do not contact the developers directly.


TWiki News, Development and Deployment
--------------------------------------

You can always find out the latest news at the TWiki home 
page at http://TWiki.org/ .

The place to collaborate on further TWiki development is at
http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Codev/ . ReadmeFirst tells you 
how to collaborate. Subscribe in WebNotify to stay up to 
date on latest development issues.

A side note in case you intend to use TWiki on your Intranet:
TWiki is successfully deployed as a collaboration tool and
dynamic Intranet tool at many major companies. You need to 
consider some important points to reach that goal. Do not 
underestimate the initial effort it takes to get a 
collaboration tool accepted within the company. Support from 
upper management is a must. A company with a culture that 
encourages information sharing is much more likely to succeed 
than one where information hoarding is the norm. There is 
also an initial catch 22 problem if you intend to use it as a 
knowledge base: "

TWiki (TM) - A Web Based Collaboration Platform
===============================================


TWiki Distribution
------------------

Version: 01 Feb 2003
Release type: Production release


What is TWiki?
--------------

TWiki is a flexible and powerful web-based collaboration 
platform that allows you to run a dynamic intranet site, a 
project development space, a document management system, a 
knowledge base, an issue tracking system and many other 
groupware application. TWiki looks and feels like a normal 
intranet or Web site. Users can freely change or create 
content from any Web browser, without requiring special 
browser plugins. 

Major companies like Sun Microsystems, Motorola, Inktomi 
and SAP depend on the TWiki platform to increase the
productivity of their engineering teams. 

Features include automatic link generation, full text 
search, authorization based on groups, Web form handling, 
email notification of changes, file attachments to Web 
pages, revision control of pages and attachments, and 
more. The server-side TWiki Plugins API provides developers 
with a simple way to build new groupware applications. 

The GPLed TWiki software and over 60 Plugins can be 
downloaded from the TWiki.org web site, http://TWiki.org/.


TWiki Distribution and License
------------------------------

TWiki is open source software and is distributed under the 
terms of the GNU General Public License. You can request 
the latest version of TWiki from http://TWiki.org/ .

The license.txt file, located in the root of the TWiki 
distribution package, shows your rights and duties on how to 
use, redistribute and/or modify it. Any redistribution of 
TWiki or it's clones MUST contain the UNMODIFIED license.txt 
file.

Please note that TWiki is not distributed under the LGPL 
(Lesser General Public Licence), which implies TWiki can 
only be used with software that is licensed under conditions 
compliant with the GPL. Embedding in proprietary software 
requires an alternative license. Contact the author for 
details.


TWiki Installation, Support
---------------------------

It is important to follow the installation instructions in
TWikiDocumentation.html located in the distribution, also at
http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/TWiki/TWikiDocumentation

Important note: Once you installed TWiki on your own system, 
make sure to add yourself to the list of TWikiInstallations 
at http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Main/TWikiInstallations . 
This helps to get more exposure --> attract more developers 
--> result in a better product.

Please add a "Powered by TWiki" logo to your TWiki home page. 
Review details in
http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Main/PoweredByTWikiLogo

TWiki is free software and does not include any support. There
is a TWiki web for support questions, run by TWiki users for
TWiki users. Visit http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Support/ if
you have any installation questions or questions about TWiki
deployment; please do not contact the developers directly.


TWiki News, Development and Deployment
--------------------------------------

You can always find out the latest news at the TWiki home 
page at http://TWiki.org/ .

The place to collaborate on further TWiki development is at
http://TWiki.org/cgi-bin/view/Codev/ . ReadmeFirst tells you 
how to collaborate. Subscribe in WebNotify to stay up to 
date on latest development issues.

A side note in case you intend to use TWiki on your Intranet:
TWiki is successfully deployed as a collaboration tool and
dynamic Intranet tool at many major companies. You need to 
consider some important points to reach that goal. Do not 
underestimate the initial effort it takes to get a 
collaboration tool accepted within the company. Support from 
upper management is a must. A company with a culture that 
encourages information sharing is much more likely to succeed 
than one where information hoarding is the norm. There is 
also an initial catch 22 problem if you intend to use it as a 
knowledge base: "

evidence_management.integrity_disclaimer: SHA-256 hash verifies byte-level storage integrity of the captured artifact; it does not independently prove that an observation is exploitable.

validation.test_name: Outdated Software Banner CVE & Template Verification
validation.methodology: Correlates fingerprinted software versions with Nmap NSE and Nuclei CVE verification templates.
validation.expected_result: Target enforces security control (CWE-1004: Security Control Weakness) and rejects insecure configuration.
validation.actual_result: A cookie has been set without the HttpOnly flag, which means that the cookie can be accessed by JavaScript. If a malicious script can be run on this page then the cookie will be accessible and can be transmitted to another site. If this is a session cookie then session hijacking may be possible.
reproduction_steps: 1. Ensure target 'http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/' is within approved Rules of Engagement allowlist.
2. Issue GET request to 'http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/' inspecting parameter/header 'PHPSESSID'.
3. Inspect response headers/body for evidence matching: Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID.
4. Compare response against the expected secure control baseline.

DISCOVERED.meaning: Scanner identified a possible issue or exposed surface; runtime reproduction has not yet been performed.
DISCOVERED.exploitability_note: Observation only — does not establish that an attacker exploited or can exploit the finding.

OBSERVATION_CONFIRMED.meaning: The observed network, protocol, or HTTP response behavior was deterministically captured in a forensic transcript.
OBSERVATION_CONFIRMED.exploitability_note: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

CONTROL_GAP_CONFIRMED.meaning: A defensive security control is demonstrably missing, weak, or misconfigured based on captured response evidence.
CONTROL_GAP_CONFIRMED.exploitability_note: Confirms a control gap was observed; it does not establish that an attacker successfully exploited it.

ATTACK_PATH_VALIDATED.meaning: A multi-step attack path combining this weakness with reachable prerequisites was validated.
ATTACK_PATH_VALIDATED.exploitability_note: Prerequisites and chaining conditions were verified.

RUNTIME_REPRODUCED.meaning: The vulnerability was actively reproduced at runtime using a deterministic non-destructive canary or probe.
RUNTIME_REPRODUCED.exploitability_note: Runtime behavior was reproduced and verified in the response transcript.

IMPACT_VERIFIED.meaning: The downstream security impact (such as unauthorized data access or execution) was directly demonstrated.
IMPACT_VERIFIED.exploitability_note: Exploitability and security impact are cryptographically proven.

REMEDIATION_VERIFIED.meaning: Subsequent retest confirmed the security control is now properly enforced.
REMEDIATION_VERIFIED.exploitability_note: Previously observed weakness has been remediated.

NOT_VULNERABLE.meaning: Testing did not establish the suspected vulnerability.

INCONCLUSIVE.meaning: Captured evidence was insufficient to confirm or rule out the issue.

BLOCKED_BY_SCOPE.meaning: Rules of Engagement (ROE) prevented active testing of this surface.
BLOCKED_BY_SCOPE.exploitability_note: Not tested due to authorization boundary.

limitations: Executed under deterministic ROE read-only safety constraints.

risk_analysis.exploitability_assessment: Control Gap / Configuration Weakness (Exploitation Not Demonstrated)
risk_analysis.business_impact: Informational or defense-in-depth hardening gap with low direct impact.

calculation_breakdown.disclaimer: TrePath Risk Priority is an internal triage metric and is never represented as an official CVSS score.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/ and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/ can leverage '[OWASP ZAP] Cookie No HttpOnly Flag' (CWE-1004) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

remediation.root_cause: CWE-1004 (Security Control Weakness) observed on http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/.
remediation.technical_remediation: Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set for all cookies.
implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/'.
2. Apply recommended control: Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set for all cookies.
3. Deploy change to staging and verify application functionality.
4. Execute TrePath deterministic retest to confirm control enforcement.
remediation.verification_procedure: Re-issue GET probe to 'http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/' and confirm ZAP-10010-10010 is no longer triggered.
remediation.functional_test: Verify authorized users and API clients can still access 'http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/' over approved transport.
remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'http://192.168.195.139/dvwa/' are rejected or redirected.

references.cwe: CWE-1004: Security Control Weakness

793.title: [OWASP ZAP] Server Leaks Information via "X-Powered-By" HTTP Response Header Field(s)
793.proof_state_meaning: The observed network, protocol, or HTTP response behavior was deterministically captured in a forensic transcript.
793.exploitability_note: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

overview.cwe_name: Protection Mechanism Failure (Missing Security Headers)
overview.affected_environment: VMware Lab Pentest Engagement (http://192.168.195.139/) (Internal Testing Lab)

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed: The web/application server is leaking information via one or more "X-Powered-By" HTTP response headers. Access to such information may facilitate attackers identifying other frameworks/components your web application is reliant upon and the vulnerabilities such components may be subject to.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to suppress "X-Powered-By" headers.

validation.expected_result: Target enforces security control (CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure (Missing Security Headers)) and rejects insecure configuration.
validation.actual_result: The web/application server is leaking information via one or more "X-Powered-By" HTTP response headers. Access to such information may facilitate attackers identifying other frameworks/components your web application is reliant upon and the vulnerabilities such components may be subject to.
reproduction_steps: 1. Ensure target 'http://192.168.195.139/' is within approved Rules of Engagement allowlist.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139/ and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/ can leverage '[OWASP ZAP] Server Leaks Information via "X-Powered-By" HTTP Response Header Field(s)' (CWE-693) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

remediation.root_cause: CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure (Missing Security Headers)) observed on http://192.168.195.139/.
remediation.technical_remediation: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to suppress "X-Powered-By" headers.
implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'http://192.168.195.139/'.
2. Apply recommended control: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to suppress "X-Powered-By" headers.
3. Deploy change to staging and verify application functionality.
4. Execute TrePath deterministic retest to confirm control enforcement.
remediation.verification_procedure: Re-issue GET probe to 'http://192.168.195.139/' and confirm ZAP-10037-10037 is no longer triggered.
remediation.functional_test: Verify authorized users and API clients can still access 'http://192.168.195.139/' over approved transport.
remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'http://192.168.195.139/' are rejected or redirected.

technical_observation.what_trepath_observed: A cookie has been set without the SameSite attribute, which means that the cookie can be sent as a result of a 'cross-site' request. The SameSite attribute is an effective counter measure to cross-site request forgery, cross-site script inclusion, and timing attacks.
technical_observation.expected_secure_behavior: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.

attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/mutillidae/index.php?do=toggle-hints&page=home.php can leverage '[OWASP ZAP] Cookie without SameSite Attribute' (CWE-1275) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

remediation.root_cause: CWE-1275 (Security Control Weakness) observed on http://192.168.195.139/mutillidae/index.php?do=toggle-hints&page=home.php.
remediation.technical_remediation: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'http://192.168.195.139/mutillidae/index.php?do=toggle-hints&page=home.php'.
2. Apply recommended control: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
3. Deploy change to staging and verify application functionality.
4. Execute TrePath deterministic retest to confirm control enforcement.
remediation.verification_procedure: Re-issue GET probe to 'http://192.168.195.139/mutillidae/index.php?do=toggle-hints&page=home.php' and confirm ZAP-10054-10054-1 is no longer triggered.
remediation.functional_test: Verify authorized users and API clients can still access 'http://192.168.195.139/mutillidae/index.php?do=toggle-hints&page=home.php' over approved transport.
remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'http://192.168.195.139/mutillidae/index.php?do=toggle-hints&page=home.php' are rejected or redirected.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to tcp://192.168.195.139:513.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to tcp://192.168.195.139:513 can leverage 'Nmap Open Service: login (513/TCP)' (CWE-200) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap

remediation.functional_test: Verify authorized users and API clients can still access 'tcp://192.168.195.139:513' over approved transport.
remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'tcp://192.168.195.139:513' are rejected or redirected.

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139//phpMyAdmin/ and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139//phpMyAdmin/ can leverage '[Nuclei] phpMyAdmin Panel - Detect' (CWE-200) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139/ and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/ can leverage '[Nuclei] WAF Detection (apachegeneric)' (CWE-200) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

attack_scenario.prerequisites: Network reachability to http://192.168.195.139/ and ability to observe or intercept HTTP traffic on the network path.
attack_scenario.abuse_narrative: An adversary with access to http://192.168.195.139/ can leverage '[Nuclei] Apache HTTP Server End-of-Life - Detect' (CWE-200) to weaken application defenses or chain with adjacent service exposures.
attack_scenario.what_was_demonstrated: Confirms the technical observation exists; does not prove active exploitation.

correlated_attack_paths.title: External Service Exposure to Version/Application Control Gap on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Adversary discovers reachable network service (PORT-OPEN-21-FTP_CONTROL) on 192.168.195.139, correlates service/version telemetry (ENUM-PROTO-MYSQL-3306), and targets application/administrative control surface (DAST-ADMIN-ACCESS-EP-00028: [ADMIN-ACCESS-001] Administrative Interface Reachable (HTTP 200) on http://192.168.195.139/phpMyAdmin/). Primary Chokepoint: Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Cleartext file transfer protocol. Migrate to SFTP or FTPS.
Bind MySQL (3306/TCP) to 127.0.0.1 or restrict network access strictly to application tier hosts.
Restrict administrative interfaces (/admin, :8080/manager) to internal management VPNs or bastion hosts and enforce MFA.

correlated_attack_paths.title: Unencrypted Transport & Authentication/Session Control Chain on 192.168.195.139
correlated_attack_paths.narrative: Traffic served over unencrypted or non-redirecting transport (HTTP-NO-HTTPS-REDIRECT) exposes authentication or session handling (DAST-BOLA-IDOR-EP-00024: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /) and compounds browser/cookie policy gaps (ZAP-10054-10054-1). Enforcing HTTPS/HSTS breaks the chain at Step 1.

steps.summary: HTTP endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirect
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Deploy and validate HTTPS, then redirect HTTP requests to the canonical HTTPS origin.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.summary: [BOLA-IDOR-001] Unauthenticated Object Identifier Parameter (`id`) Accepted on /
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Enforce server-side object-level authorization checks verifying that the authenticated caller owns the requested resource ID.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

steps.phase: Session Token / Browser Policy Hardening Gap
steps.mitigation_chokepoint: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.
steps.blast_radius: Authenticated User Sessions & Credentials in Transit

remediation.technical_remediation: Review server configuration, apply latest vendor security patches, and restrict unauthenticated access.
implementation_steps: 1. Locate configuration or route handler serving 'http://192.168.195.139/'.
2. Apply recommended control: Review server configuration, apply latest vendor security patches, and restrict unauthenticated access.
3. Deploy change to staging and verify application functionality.

remediation.verification_procedure: Re-issue GET probe to 'http://192.168.195.139/' and confirm NUCLEI-APACHE-HTTPD-EOL is no longer triggered.
remediation.functional_test: Verify authorized users and API clients can still access 'http://192.168.195.139/' over approved transport.
remediation.negative_boundary_test: Verify unencrypted, unauthenticated, or malformed requests to 'http://192.168.195.139/' are rejected or redirected.

Appendix B: TWiki Development Timeline

01-Feb-2003 Release (Beijing)

  • 18 Jan 2003 - PeterThoeny
    • Support for /bin/view/Web.TopicName topic view URL (besides the default /bin/view/Web/TopicName URL); useful for InterwikiPlugin links like TWiki:Codev.ReadmeFirst
  • 31 Dec 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • Enhanced Plugin API to manipulate topic data with new functions in TWikiFuncModule: readTopicText, saveTopicText, setTopicEditLock, checkTopicEditLock
  • 31 Dec 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • New %NOAUTOLINK% setting in the TWikiPreferences to disable the auto-linking of WikiWords
  • 29 Dec 2002 - AndreaSterbini, PeterThoeny, RichardDonkin, SvenDowideit
    • New Plugin hooks registrationHandler, beforeEditHandler, afterEditHandler, beforeSaveHandler, writeHeaderHandler, redirectCgiQueryHandler, getSessionValueHandler, setSessionValueHandler
  • 30 Nov 2002 - RichardDonkin
    • Internationalization ('I18N') support 8-bit character sets in WikiWords, such as ISO-8859-15, KOI8-R
  • 25 Nov 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • Include previous topic revision with %INCLUDE{ "OtherTopic" rev="1.2" }%
  • 15 Nov 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • The Go box understands also URLs, useful for special TWikiSkins handling
  • 08 Nov 2002 - ColasNahaboo, RichardDonkin
    • In

Appendix B: TWiki Development Timeline

01-Feb-2003 Release (Beijing)

  • 18 Jan 2003 - PeterThoeny
    • Support for /bin/view/Web.TopicName topic view URL (besides the default /bin/view/Web/TopicName URL); useful for InterwikiPlugin links like TWiki:Codev.ReadmeFirst
  • 31 Dec 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • Enhanced Plugin API to manipulate topic data with new functions in TWikiFuncModule: readTopicText, saveTopicText, setTopicEditLock, checkTopicEditLock
  • 31 Dec 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • New %NOAUTOLINK% setting in the TWikiPreferences to disable the auto-linking of WikiWords
  • 29 Dec 2002 - AndreaSterbini, PeterThoeny, RichardDonkin, SvenDowideit
    • New Plugin hooks registrationHandler, beforeEditHandler, afterEditHandler, beforeSaveHandler, writeHeaderHandler, redirectCgiQueryHandler, getSessionValueHandler, setSessionValueHandler
  • 30 Nov 2002 - RichardDonkin
    • Internationalization ('I18N') support 8-bit character sets in WikiWords, such as ISO-8859-15, KOI8-R
  • 25 Nov 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • Include previous topic revision with %INCLUDE{ "OtherTopic" rev="1.2" }%
  • 15 Nov 2002 - PeterThoeny
    • The Go box understands also URLs, useful for special TWikiSkins handling
  • 08 Nov 2002 - ColasNahaboo, RichardDonkin
    • In
